$comment: Authorization policy for anything the agent does that reaches outside the workspace. The default answer to 'may I write?' is NO. This file is the only place that answer can change.
principles: Reading is free; writing is earned.
Authorization is per-action and per-session. Approving one issue does not approve the next.
An action is only 'done' when the provider confirms it. An unconfirmed write is reported as INCONCLUSIVE.
Never assign work to a human the agent picked itself.
Prefer the safe environment. If a safe environment does not exist, that is a blocker, not a reason to use production.

levels.workspace-only: May write inside the repository working tree only. Never outside it.
levels.explicit: Requires the user to authorise this specific action in this session.
levels.explicit-named-assignee: Requires the user to name the account, or to state a rule the agent can apply mechanically.
levels.non-production-only: Permitted only against an environment the profile marks as non-production.
levels.prohibited-by-default: Refuse. May only proceed if the user restates the request after being told the risk.

fs.write_test_file.note: Adding or updating tests inside the repo is normal work.

fs.write_source_file.note: Changing product code to make a test pass is forbidden separately; see forbidden_patterns.

drive.upload_evidence.note: Evidence may contain screenshots of real data. Confirm before uploading.

load_test.execute.note: Load traffic is indistinguishable from an attack. Needs an owner's sign-off and a non-production target.

security_scan.active.note: Active scanning of a host requires authorisation from whoever owns that host.

environment_rules.$comment_markers: These are heuristics for warning, not for permission. A host is treated as non-production only when the repository profile explicitly says so.
environment_rules.why: Mistaking staging for production costs a wasted question. Mistaking production for staging costs an incident.

forbidden_patterns.rule: Never modify product behaviour, assertions-under-test, or configuration in order to make a failing test pass.
forbidden_patterns.instead: Record a finding. A failing test that reflects a real defect is the deliverable.

forbidden_patterns.rule: Never create a screenshot, log, trace or result that did not come from an actual run.
forbidden_patterns.instead: Report the status as BLOCKED or NOT_APPLICABLE.

forbidden_patterns.rule: Never report an external write as successful without a provider response containing an identifier.
forbidden_patterns.instead: Report INCONCLUSIVE and record what was attempted.

forbidden_patterns.rule: Never choose a human to assign work to based on git blame, CODEOWNERS or seniority.
forbidden_patterns.instead: Leave unassigned and tell the user who the candidates are.

forbidden_patterns.rule: Never write credentials, tokens or keys into state, reports or issue bodies.
forbidden_patterns.instead: The redaction pass masks known shapes; do not deliberately capture secret material as evidence.
